# ferentin_mcp_route (Resource)

MCP route — sends an MCP server that a managed device starts through Ferentin.

* A **remote** target (`host`, `url_prefix`) is rewritten to the gateway (`mechanism` `rewrite_to_gateway`): to `steer_to_url`, or the scope's own gateway when it is unset.
* A **local** target (`package`, `argv_contains`) is wrapped in `ferentin-mcp` (`mechanism` `shim_wrap`), so its tool calls pass through Ferentin.

In the unified MCP policy model a route is what an endpoint MCP rule's `steer` action became. Allowing or denying a server is not a route's job: that is `ferentin_mcp_policy`, with device `targets`. A route never grants.

The platform refuses a route that sends a server somewhere other than where an enabled route already sends it, in an overlapping scope and app (`route_conflict`), and a `steer_to_url` that is not this tenant's MCP gateway or one of its edge sites. Changes reach devices on the tenant's next activation.

## Import

```
terraform import ferentin_mcp_route.example <tenant_id>/<route_id>
```

An import has no configured spelling of `target.values`, so it takes the platform's canonical form. Where that differs from your config's spelling, the first plan after import shows `target.values` changing to it; applying it changes nothing on the platform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# MCP routes send an MCP server a managed device starts through Ferentin. In the
# unified MCP policy model a route is what an endpoint MCP rule's "steer" became;
# allowing or denying a server is ferentin_mcp_policy's job, with device targets.

# The device group the scoped route targets. Declared here so the snippet stands
# on its own; see ferentin_device_group for the full resource.
resource "ferentin_device_group" "engineering" {
  name   = "engineering"
  source = "manual"
}

# Remote MCP server: rewrite it to a route on this tenant's MCP gateway, for
# engineering's devices only. steer_to_url must be this tenant's gateway or one
# of its edge sites; leave it unset to use the scope's own gateway.
resource "ferentin_mcp_route" "github_through_gateway" {
  name = "github-through-gateway"

  target = {
    kind   = "host"
    values = ["api.githubcopilot.com"]
  }
  steer_to_url     = "https://acme.mcp.ferentin.net/v1/github"
  device_group_ids = [ferentin_device_group.engineering.group_id]
}

# Local (stdio) MCP server: wrap one npm package in ferentin-mcp, so its tool
# calls pass through Ferentin. A local route has no URL.
resource "ferentin_mcp_route" "wrap_internal_package" {
  name        = "wrap-internal-mcp-package"
  description = "Govern the internal MCP server wherever it runs"

  target = {
    kind   = "package"
    values = ["npm:@acme/internal-mcp"]
  }

  # Only in this MCP client's config files.
  app_bundle_ids = ["com.anthropic.claudefordesktop"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Route name, unique within the tenant. 1-255 characters, with no leading or trailing whitespace (the platform trims it).
- `target` (Attributes) What the route selects on a device. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--target))

### Optional

- `app_bundle_ids` (List of String) Narrow the route to the config files of these MCP **clients** (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) by macOS bundle identifier, e.g. `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop`. Empty or unset = every app. At most 64.
- `description` (String)
- `device_group_ids` (List of String) Device groups the route applies to — reference `ferentin_device_group.<name>.group_id`. Empty or unset = **every device in the tenant**. At most 64.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether devices apply the route. Default `true`.
- `steer_to_url` (String) Remote targets only: the gateway route to rewrite the server to, for example `https://<tenant-short-name>.mcp.ferentin.net/v1/<route>`. It must be this tenant's MCP gateway or one of its edge sites, and `https://`. Unset: the scope's own gateway. Refused on a `package` or `argv_contains` target, which is wrapped in `ferentin-mcp` and has no URL.
- `tenant_id` (String)

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_modified_by` (String) Provenance of the most recent writer. Divergence from `managed_by` is the drift signal.
- `managed_by` (String) Provenance of the original creator (`iac` for this provider). Immutable after create.
- `mechanism` (String) Read-only. `rewrite_to_gateway` for a remote target, `shim_wrap` for a local one.
- `route_id` (String)
- `stored_target_values` (List of String) Read-only. `target.values` as the platform stores them, after canonicalisation. A console edit shows up as a change here and in `target.values` on the next plan.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version` (Number) Optimistic-concurrency version, sent as `If-Match` on update and delete so a concurrent console edit is rejected with 412 rather than overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `target`

Required:

- `kind` (String) `host` or `url_prefix` (a remote server's address), or `package` or `argv_contains` (a local server's command line).
- `values` (List of String) Values to match, interpreted per `kind`. 1-64 entries. `host` values are bare hostnames (no scheme, port or path); `package` values are one registry-qualified id each.

The platform stores them in the canonical spelling a steer rule's values take. Terraform keeps your spelling here and the platform's in `stored_target_values`, so canonicalisation does not show as drift.
